races.title: State House, District 12
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Chris Humphrey
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 12 (Lenoir, Greene, Jones counties) since January 2019. Former Lenoir County commissioner for eight years and La Grange Town Council member for three. Chairs the House Insurance Committee. Graduated from UNC-Chapel Hill with a political science degree.
cands.gaps: We could not find Humphrey's occupation outside public office, his exact birthplace, or the year he was born. The pages we read showed no bills he sponsored or actions he took, and no statements from him, on data centers, homestead taxes, land buying by out-of-state or foreign owners, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or notable endorsements. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. His campaign site mentions state budget funding for local projects, but we could only read the headline, not the article.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign website says he was born and raised in Eastern North Carolina, and he has served in local and state office there and lives in Kinston.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State House member since 2019, with service on the Appropriations and Finance committees. Previously a Lenoir County commissioner for eight years and a La Grange Town Council member for three years.
qual.why: Seven years of legislative service plus earlier local elected office is directly relevant to writing law and the state budget. His non-political career is not documented in the pages available, so the score stays below the top of the range. Committee chairmanships were not counted.

cands.name: Don Hardy
cands.bio: Two-term mayor of Kinston, North Carolina, and U.S. Navy veteran. Says he is a law enforcement officer with nearly 20 years at local, county and federal levels, including seven years with the Kinston Police Department. Ran as a Democrat for NC House District 12 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter-guide recommendations from two informal 'Sway' voting groups: Better Future NC (Cam Pruette) and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (Tevin Davis).

cands.gaps: We found no independent reporting on Hardy's record as mayor, so his claims of securing tens of millions in state and federal funding, and the dates of his mayoral terms, are unconfirmed. His birth year and any move to or from North Carolina were not found. We found no stated position on data centers, development, growth limits, property taxes, out-of-state or investor land buying, guns, abortion, or immigration and H-1B policy. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no news controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign website says he was born and raised in Kinston and has lived there nearly his whole life, apart from four years in the Navy.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Two-term mayor of Kinston, Navy veteran, and a self-described law enforcement officer of nearly 20 years (seven with Kinston Police). Sits on the NC League of Municipalities and National League of Cities boards and the NC Global TransPark Authority board. No prior legislative service found.
qual.why: Local elected office (mayor) and long public-safety work put him in the middle band. He has no state legislative service or direct budget-writing career, so he does not reach the high band.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he supports higher teacher pay and sustained K-12 public education investment, backing the priorities of the state Superintendent of Public Instruction. He gave no position on vouchers, charters or school choice.

back-police-order.evidence: Says he will support good policy and adequate resources for police officers, firefighters, EMS personnel and 911 telecommunicators.
